contentText:
A new nationwide study found that in-school cellphone bans can lead to modest improvements in learning. Now, researchers want to understand whether kids' phone use outside the classroom might contribute to the rest of students' learning loss - using the conditions of Meta's multibillion-dollar settlement from earlier this year.

Banning cellphones in schools has the equivalent effect of adding one to two weeks of school to the academic year, accounting for about half of the learning loss students experienced in the US between 2013 and the 2020 covid-19 pandemic, according to the study carried out by researchers from Harvard University and Da …
